task.title: PRODUCTDELETE
task.spec:
You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

Merchants delete discontinued products all the time, and every time they do, something breaks. A cart that held the product can't be opened any more, and an order that included it can't be read by the merchant or by the customer who placed it.

Deleting a product (DELETE /api/v1/private/product/{id}) must not break carts or orders:

- Carts that held the product: GET /api/v1/cart/{code} returns the cart without it, with its subtotal, total and quantity worked out from the products left. A cart whose only product was deleted is returned with no products and a total of 0. The cart can still be changed (PUT /api/v1/cart/{code}, POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/multi) and checked out; the deleted product is never ordered or charged. Trying to add the deleted product to a cart gives HTTP 404 Not Found.
- Orders that included the product: GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}, GET /api/v1/private/orders, GET /api/v1/auth/orders/{id} and GET /api/v1/auth/orders keep working, and show the product as it was bought: its sku, name, ordered quantity, price and subtotal, exactly as before it was deleted. The order's totals don't change. The order's status can still be changed (PUT /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/status).
- Checkout keeps working for every cart, whatever products have been deleted before.
- GET /api/v2/product/{sku} for a deleted product gives HTTP 404 Not Found. Deleting a product changes nothing about any other product.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.

runs.report:
## Scope and repository confirmation

The task belongs to this Shopizer checkout. The requested API paths are implemented under `sm-shop`, with catalog/cart/order persistence and services in `sm-core`, `sm-core-model`, and `sm-shop-model`. No linked GitHub issue or existing task-specific implementation was supplied; repository history contains only the baseline commit.

## Evidence

- Product deletion is handled by `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v2/product/ProductApiV2.java` (`DELETE /private/product/{id}`), delegating to `productCommonFacade.deleteProduct`.
- Product deletion ultimately calls `ProductServiceImpl.delete`; the product entity is removed after catalog-owned relationships are handled (`sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/business/services/catalog/product/ProductServiceImpl.java`).
- `ShoppingCartItem` persists `PRODUCT_ID` and `SKU`, but its `Product product` reference is `@Transient` (`sm-core-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/shoppingcart/ShoppingCartItem.java`). Cart reload hydrates that transient reference by SKU in `ShoppingCartServiceImpl.getPopulatedItem`.
- Cart hydration currently calls `productService.getBySku`; a missing product raises `ServiceException`, and the surrounding cart load fails. The intended obsolete-item branch only handles a null product and then marks the whole cart obsolete (`sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/business/services/shoppingcart/ShoppingCartServiceImpl.java`).
- The current readable cart mapper dereferences `item.getProduct()` and includes every persisted line item, then recalculates totals (`sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/mapper/cart/ReadableShoppingCartMapper.java`). This is a direct failure point after deletion.
- Cart updates and multi-item updates resolve requested SKUs through `ShoppingCartFacadeImpl.fetchProduct` / `createCartItems`; missing products are converted to not-found failures (`sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/controller/shoppingCart/facade/ShoppingCartFacadeImpl.java`). This existing boundary should be preserved and covered by tests.
- `OrderProduct` already snapshots SKU, product name, quantity, and one-time charge without a catalog-product relationship (`sm-core-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/order/orderproduct/OrderProduct.java`).
- Order response mapping still attempts to reload the catalog product by SKU. `ReadableOrderProductMapper` and the legacy `ReadableOrderProductPopulator` throw when that lookup fails, although the snapshot fields needed by the API are already present (`sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/mapper/order/ReadableOrderProductMapper.java`, `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/populator/order/ReadableOrderProductPopulator.java`).
- The private and authenticated order endpoints delegate to `OrderFacadeImpl.getReadableOrder` and list conversion, which invoke the legacy order-product populator (`sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v1/order/OrderApi.java`, `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/controller/order/facade/OrderFacadeImpl.java`).
- V2 product lookup already routes through `ProductFacadeV2Impl.getProductByCode`, whose missing-SKU path is intended to produce `ResourceNotFoundException`; this should be regression-tested after deletion (`sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/facade/product/ProductFacadeV2Impl.java`).
- Existing API coverage is concentrated in `sm-shop/src/test/java/com/salesmanager/test/shop/integration/cart/ShoppingCartAPIIntegrationTest.java`; no deletion-survival cart/order scenario was found.

## Problem and scope

Product deletion currently invalidates persisted cart line items during hydration and makes historical order rendering dependent on the live catalog. The implementation should make carts resilient by removing deleted-product lines from the usable cart, persisting that cleanup or otherwise ensuring subsequent reads/updates/checkout ignore them, and recalculating quantity, subtotal, total, and checkout inputs from remaining products. New additions must reject deleted SKUs with HTTP 404. Historical orders must render from their immutable `OrderProduct` snapshot fields and retain stored totals/status behavior, without requiring a live catalog product.

Scope includes cart service hydration/mutation/checkout paths, cart API mapping and calculations, order product mapping used by both detail and list endpoints, product lookup behavior, and integration/regression tests. Do not alter unrelated products or change normal live-product behavior.

## Acceptance checks

1. Create a cart with a target product and another product; delete the target; GET `/api/v1/cart/{code}` succeeds and contains only the remaining product with correct quantity, subtotal, and total.
2. Delete the only cart product; GET succeeds with an empty product list, quantity zero, and total zero.
3. After deletion, PUT `/api/v1/cart/{code}`, POST `/api/v1/cart/{code}/multi`, and checkout succeed for remaining valid items; the deleted item is never ordered or charged.
4. Adding the deleted SKU through the supported cart-add and multi-item paths returns HTTP 404.
5. An order containing the product remains readable through private/authenticated detail and list endpoints; SKU, name, quantity, unit price, subtotal, and order totals remain unchanged after deletion.
6. Updating order status through `PUT /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/status` still succeeds after product deletion.
7. Checkout succeeds for carts containing stale deleted-product rows and creates no order line for the deleted product.
8. `GET /api/v2/product/{sku}` returns HTTP 404 for the deleted SKU, while another product remains retrievable.
9. Existing cart/order/product tests continue to pass.

## Likely implementation areas

- `ShoppingCartServiceImpl`: tolerate missing catalog products, remove or mark only those line items unusable, and avoid treating a partially stale cart as entirely obsolete.
- `ReadableShoppingCartMapper` and calculation/checkout paths: filter stale items and calculate solely from valid items, including the empty-cart case.
- `ShoppingCartFacadeImpl`: retain explicit not-found behavior for new additions and ensure update/multi/checkout paths cannot reintroduce stale items.
- `ReadableOrderProductMapper`, `ReadableOrderProductPopulator`, and `OrderFacadeImpl`: treat live catalog enrichment as optional; always map snapshot fields and omit only unavailable enrichment such as current product metadata/images.
- Add focused integration tests under the existing cart/order test packages, likely using the established `ServicesTestSupport` fixtures.

## Complexity and routing

Medium complexity. The behavior is clear and routine implementation choices can follow existing service, mapper, exception, and integration-test conventions; no separate design approval is required. Main risk is covering every cart mutation and checkout path plus both legacy order list/detail conversion paths.
